references.text: A similar event where Moses strikes the rock to give water to the people, but here he is rebuked for striking instead of speaking to the rock.
Moses reminds the people how God led them through the wilderness and gave them water from the hard rock.
The psalmist describes how God split rocks in the wilderness and gave the people plenty of water to drink.
The psalmist praises God for opening the rock so that water flowed out into the wilderness.
The psalmist describes God's power that turned the rock into a source of water.
Isaiah refers to how God gave his people water from the rock when he led them through the wilderness.
Paul interprets the rock as a picture of Christ, the spiritual rock that followed the Israelites and gave them spiritual drink.
The actual execution of the command to strike the rock for water (with theological contrast in Moses' attitude).
Contrast between God's command to trust Him (Exodus) and Moses' anger/doubt before he breaks God's word (Numbers).
The critical contrast in God's command: 'strike' (Exodus) versus 'speak' (Numbers), which explains Moses' error.
